title: Notifications and Awareness: A Field Study of Alert Usage and Preferences
claim: A two-week workplace email study found varied effects when notifications were removed, including more self-checking for some users.
limitations: Older email study; not a trial of Tandem, Slack or a universal notification default.

title: Productive, Anxious, Lonely — 24 Hours Without Push Notifications
claim: Thirty volunteers disabled alerts for one day; reported benefits coexisted with anxiety and reduced social connection.
limitations: Small volunteer sample, short intervention and self-reports; no population productivity effect established.

title: Batching smartphone notifications can improve well-being
publisher: Fitz et al., Computers in Human Behavior
claim: Randomized smartphone study with 237 participants compared batching schedules and alert suppression; effects depended on the intervention.
limitations: Not a workplace-chat product comparison; outcomes include self-report. Search summaries were inconsistent on productivity, so no precise productivity claim is used.

title: Show HN: Dock — Slack minus the bloat, tax, and 90-day memory loss
claim: Respondents describe external partners, integrations and mobile notifications as reasons a chat replacement may fail to win adoption.
limitations: Self-selected launch feedback, promotional context and disputed claims; comments are not verified product documentation or representative demand.

title: Show HN: Colanode, open-source and local-first Slack and Notion alternative
claim: Discussion includes disagreement over self-hosted mobile notifications, operating effort and service funding.
limitations: Pricing allegations are historical anecdotes; current vendor documentation is required for comparison.

title: The current (sad) state of self-hosted chat apps
claim: Participants report setup, guest access, push and casual-threading friction; replies dispute several original claims.
limitations: Do not carry older feature, price or licensing allegations forward as current facts; includes promotional replies.

title: Colanode repository and architecture
claim: Project documents local SQLite reads/writes with background sync and a server stack including Postgres, Redis and file storage.
limitations: Maintainer-described architecture; no independent performance, durability or mobile validation performed.

title: Local-first software: You own your data, in spite of the cloud
claim: Explains offline access and durable user ownership as stronger requirements than an optimistic interface or server cache.
limitations: Research/design position with prototypes, not evidence that every chat app needs CRDTs or federation.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
claim: Provides testable accessibility criteria including focus visibility, target size, reflow, authentication and media alternatives.
limitations: Standard used as a design target; this research does not establish legal compliance or certify Tandem.

title: Using GitHub in Slack
claim: Official integration groups issue and pull-request updates in threads and maintains current context.
limitations: Documents GitHub's Slack app; does not establish compatibility with Tandem's partial Slack API.

title: Hide a person in Slack
claim: Slack supports hiding people and suppressing banner notifications; badges and shared-huddle behavior have specified exceptions.
limitations: Hiding is not equivalent to preventing contact; avoid repeating older claims that no person-level control exists.

title: Security for AI features in Slack
claim: Slack says native AI respects request-time user access and does not use customer data to train LLMs.
limitations: Vendor security statement, not an independent audit; third-party apps and other products need their own review.

title: How Slack protects your data when using machine learning and AI
claim: Distinguishes traditional ML based on derived signals from generative AI and describes workspace opt-out.
limitations: Do not use this older explanation for present pricing or bundling; vendor account of its own controls.

title: Export your data from Google Chat
claim: Personal and organization exports have different coverage, including exclusions for certain work/school or external spaces.
limitations: An export's existence does not imply complete source history or a ready Tandem import adapter.

title: Learn about message history for conversations
claim: Conversation retention can be governed by the organization that started an external conversation.
limitations: Applies to described Google Chat configurations; no claim that every external-collaboration platform behaves identically.
